This is going to be expensive.�� Compare BMW N57 Engine Quotes See the Failure Timeline 128k First knock 133k Failure mileage �6,800 Engine only route �8,500 Final cost 18 mo Warranty Case summary A high-mileage 630d with a knock that should not have been driven. The owner first heard a deep knocking at around 128,000 miles. It began as a short cold-start noise, then became constant within six weeks. By the time the engine management light flashed on the M6, the bottom end was already in serious trouble. Vehicle BMW 630d Gran Turismo G32 Year 2016 Engine N57D30 � 3.0-litre 6-cylinder diesel First symptom 128,000 miles Failure 133,000 miles Service history Independent specialist, then DIY oil changes Disclaimer: This is an illustrative representative scenario based on common N57 failure patterns, Engines Market 2025 quote-request data, workshop consensus, and known failure-pattern data. Individual outcomes vary. Early warning The clue was already in the oil. A deep rod-knock sound is not the same as normal diesel clatter. In this case, the owner also noticed metallic glitter in the oil � a serious warning sign for bearing-shell wear. Stage 1 Cold-start knock Deep rhythmic noise for around 10 seconds, then quieter once warm. Stage 2 Knock under load The sound became louder and more consistent during acceleration. Stage 3 Metal in oil Copper and silver glitter suggested bearing-shell material circulating through the oil. If an N57 develops a deep bottom-end knock, do not keep driving it. Every journey can increase crankshaft journal scoring and reduce the chance of a repairable rebuild. Failure timeline 5,000 miles from first knock to recovery. The knock started around 128,000 miles and ended with a flashing engine management light at 133,000 miles. The car was recovered to a BMW specialist in Birmingham. What the owner was told �Probably just the injectors settling.� The car still drove, so the warning was underestimated. What was actually happening Bearing-shell wear was producing metal contamination and likely scoring the crankshaft journals. �The car still drove, but every journey sounded worse than the last.� Symptom 1 Gradual loss of power over 3�4 weeks Symptom 2 Deep rhythmic knock, louder under load Recovery Flashing EML on the M6 Workshop diagnosis The oil filter confirmed bottom-end damage. The specialist drained the oil, cut open the oil filter, and found copper and silver particles visible to the naked eye. An oil analysis then confirmed elevated copper, lead, and iron. Copper 147 ppm � bearing shell wear Lead 89 ppm � bearing shell wear Iron 62 ppm � crankshaft journal scoring Crank journals Cylinders 3, 4, and 5 scored Inspection Sump drop recommended at �450 Conclusion Crankshaft bearing failure Specialist verdict The crank journals were almost certainly scored beyond repair. Rebuilding would only be viable if the crank was still saveable. Replacement options Used, reconditioned, or new BMW engine- The page should present this as an interactive decision tool. Metal from the bearing shells could circulate through the oil pump and turbo oil supply. A new engine paired with contaminated old components can become an expensive repeat failure. Path B Replace oil pump and turbo preventatively at the same time. �8,500 �6,800 engine + �800 pump + �900 turbo. Both risks reduced upfront. The key question was whether the crankshaft could be reground or whether the scoring was beyond limits. Rebuild existing engine Path 1 �4,500��6,500 if the crank is saveable. Timeline: 14�21 days. Pump + turbo Preventative work The owner replaced both to reduce post-repair failure risk. Low Risk tolerance The owner preferred a higher upfront repair over a second failure months later. Full documentation Resale confidence Documentation later helped the car sell for a stronger price. �8,500 Total paid Engine, oil pump, turbo, and fitting included. Reconditioned engine + preventative oil pump and turbo Final verdict The decision balanced vehicle value, warranty protection, debris contamination risk, and resale confidence. Outcome What happened after the repair- The owner paid more upfront, but avoided repeat engine-related issues and sold the car with full documentation. But friends who bought used engines had failures within a year. I sold the car for �11,000 because I had full documentation." Lessons learned The cheapest diagnostic could have changed the whole outcome. If your N57 has over 80,000 miles, an oil analysis at the next service can flag elevated copper or lead before the crankshaft becomes unsaveable. If you already have a knock, go straight to a specialist and do not drive it. Oil analysis �80��120 Early warning that can detect elevated wear metals before catastrophic bearing damage. Preventative bearing replacement �2,500��4,000 If caught early, the crank journals are more likely to be saveable. After catastrophic failure �6,500��7,500+ Car off road for 8+ days, with oil pump and turbo contamination risk. An �80 oil analysis at 128,000 miles could have detected elevated copper levels. Instead, the owner paid �8,500 after the bearing failure became catastrophic.
